title: S163 camera-follow tests broken on main — 6/13 fail after S163-g revert
summary: Full unit suite on origin/main (HEAD 98b26bc) shows **6 / 1867 tests failing**, all in `examples/kaboom-crew/tests/unit/camera-follow-system.test.ts`. The source file's top-of-file comment confirms the cause: 'S163-g revert: every iteration of damped follow ... produced visible doubling/jitter in playtest. Until we can debug the engine-side pipeline interaction safely, this system is a NO-OP for follow + only adjusts the camera's orthographicSize.' The dev intentionally reverted the follow logic to fix jitter, but DIDN'T update the unit tests that assert the camera moves toward the bomber — so they now assert behaviour the system no longer provides. Second time in 24 h that a sprint shipped with red tests on main (previous: S158 voice-synth death-contour test, addressed in PR #200). The qa-intake auto-merge CI gate clearly isn't running `npm run test` against the merged PR head, OR is treating failures as non-blocking; worth checking the gate config.
repro: Failing cases: 'follow mode snaps onto bomber position', 'centre mode locks to arena centre', 'missing target → falls back to arena centre', 'damping approaches target gradually', 'large arena + bomber near corner → camera follows toward corner', 'spectate mode follows the spectateTargetId entity'.
Read `examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/camera-follow-system.ts` top comment — explicitly states the system is now a NO-OP for follow.
expected: Either (a) update the tests to assert the new behaviour: in `follow` / `spectate` / `centre` modes the camera Transform stays at its scene-authored position, only `Camera.orthographicSize` changes; OR (b) restore the follow logic + the tests pass as they originally did. Whichever path, the full unit suite should be green on every merged main commit. CI should block merges that drop tests below green.
actual: main has 6 red tests. Future contributors running `npm run test` see a failure cascade that's actually expected, which trains them to ignore red — exactly the wrong signal. The S163-g revert was the right call (jitter was a real playtest issue), but the test housekeeping wasn't done in the same commit.
